title: Manual Grasparatus: A nifty tool for presenting real objects in fMRI research
author: Nowik, Styrkowiec, et al.

steps.title: Assemble Grasparatus device
steps.instruction: Construct the MR‑compatible Grasparatus from the two rotating drums, side panels, and conveyor belt, mounting them on supporting legs that attach to the scanner bed; optionally attach a front shield to block background view.

steps.title: Prepare stimulus belts
steps.instruction: Create fabric belts 4.4 m long and 20 cm wide, cover them with Velcro strips, and attach stimuli as follows: for the main study, fasten 96 objects (six sets of 8 tools + 8 non‑tools) with strands along the middle of each stimulus, spacing them ≈16 cm apart in a pseudorandom order; for the control study, attach tools and plastic objects only with Velcro strips, orienting them for comfortable functional grasp and allowing denser packing. Belts can be exchanged between experimental runs.

steps.title: Mount device on scanner bed
steps.instruction: Place the assembled Grasparatus on the scanner bed using its fixing legs, position it above the participant’s legs/hips so the front of the drum is reachable by the participant’s hands outside the bore, and secure the chosen stimulus belt to the conveyor belt.

steps.title: Support participant’s arms
steps.instruction: Have the participant lie in the scanner, then support the upper arms with extremity‑positioning cushions and either a hemicylindrical arm brace with Velcro straps or simple Velcro belts to keep the arms close to the torso, minimizing shoulder and head movement.

steps.title: Deliver stimuli during fMRI
steps.instruction: The experimenter, wearing headphones, receives auditory cues that dictate trial timing, then manually rotates the belt using the cloth handles sutured to the side of the conveyor belt to present one stimulus per trial in the pre‑ordered sequence, monitoring participant responses throughout.

steps.title: Manage long belts (optional)
steps.instruction: If using very long stimulus belts, assign an additional person to hold or fold the early and mid‑segment portions of the belt that have already been delivered.
